reuse.why: Extends getDateWithSkippedWeekend and adds shared isNonWorkingDay/skipsWeekendOccurrences, but the new getDatesInRange and the updated getUpcomingDates and schedule-template each still compose the skip-vs-move decision themselves instead of calling one shared day-resolution function.

duplication.why: The 'daily skip / move / leave' dispatch now exists in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template's local solveWeekendDate, and dropping non-working daily occurrences is implemented twice in different shapes (getNextWeekdayOccurrence with a 14-take window, getUpcomingDates with a count*7 over-fetch).

placement.why: Weekend/holiday rules sit in shared/schedules.ts and the handler in schedules/app.ts as the tree does, though schedule-template grows its own private weekend helper instead of using a shared one.

scope.why: Edits stay on weekend/holiday handling, the new handler, the type and tests; the rule-utils data additions are needed to carry frequency and holidays.

maintainability.why: Each future rule change must be applied at four dispatch sites with differing look-ahead constants (14, count*7, 14-day padding), so the sites can drift apart.

bypasses_abstraction.where: schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange, and budget/schedule-template.ts solveWeekendDate, decide skip vs move locally around getDateWithSkippedWeekend/isNonWorkingDay

disguised_duplication.where: schedule-template's solveWeekendDate repackages the same skipWeekend ? getDateWithSkippedWeekend : date ternary used in getNextDate/getUpcomingDates; the daily-skip filter appears as getNextWeekdayOccurrence in shared/schedules.ts and as an over-fetch .filter in getUpcomingDates

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains a daily-schedule special branch; getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template's solveWeekendDate each re-dispatch skip/move outside a shared function
